conventions: `וְעַתָּה` at a clause head is divided by sense and not by position: `עַתָּה` takes the *now* that writes its own lexeme, and the waw takes whatever other connective the ASV has written beside it, whichever order the two words stand in. JOB.42.5 *But now* and JOB.42.8 *Now therefore* are one construction, and in the second the two units cross under rule 25. Rule 51 is the ground: distance from the waw, and the side of the clause a word falls on, are not evidence about which morpheme a connective belongs to.

The idiom `נָשָׂא פָּנִים` → *accept* is fused where its morphemes are contiguous and split where they are not, which is rule 30's contiguity condition and not an inconsistency. JOB.42.8 `אִם־פָּנָיו אֶשָּׂא` → *him will I accept* is one `noncompositional` unit; JOB.42.9 `וַיִּשָּׂא יְהוָה אֶת־פְּנֵי אִיּוֹב` → *and Jehovah accepted Job* has the subject and the object marker standing between the two morphemes, so rule 2 splits it and `פְּנֵי` is `unrepresented`, as `גָּדַל ... מִן` → *exceeded* leaves its preposition. BSB attaches the noun to its phrase in both places; that is the documented convention difference behind the JOB.42.9 disagreement, not an error.

JOB.42.3 writes two `וְלֹא` + finite-verb clauses that the ASV recasts differently, and they are aligned differently on that ground alone. *that which I understood not* writes an antecedent and a relative together, which is rule 46's headless shape, so both English words join the verb's own unit and that waw is `unrepresented`; *which I knew not* writes a bare relative after an antecedent the ASV has already written, so rule 17 gives the *which* to the waw. Read what the ASV supplied before reading the pair as a split.
report: Checked all 31 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end for the `added` units the table is blind to. Twenty-nine groups are context differences the source licenses: `הָיָה` as the presentative frame in v7 against the possessive *had* of v12-13 (rule 43); the dative and possessive `לְ`s left unrepresented against the `לְ` that carries *had* in the verbless relative clause of v10; `אֶל`, `בְּ`, `עַל`, `מִן`, `כְּ` rendered variously by the ASV; `אֶחָד` as a determiner in v11 against the substantival rectum of v14; the two gapped-comparative *hath*s of v7 and v8, which are treated identically.

Real split, patched: `וְעַתָּה`. JOB.42.5 renders it *But now* and gives *now* to the adverb and the connective to the waw; JOB.42.8 renders it *Now therefore* and gave *Now* to the waw and *therefore* to the adverb. Nothing in the source licenses the difference, only the order in which the ASV wrote the two English words. Rule 51 settles that position is not what assigns a connective to a waw, rule 25 permits the crossing, and rule 11 assigns a function word to the morpheme whose sense it carries, so JOB.42.8 now gives *Now* to `עַתָּה` and *therefore* to the waw. The competing position-based reading is named in the verse's notes under rule 8.

Contract error, patched: JOB.42.7's frame complementizer. The verse pass moved *that* from `הָיָה` onto the apodosis waw on the strength of rule 45's bolded waw sentence, but that rule's own qualification governs: the ASV writes the *that* immediately after *And it was so* and ahead of the temporal clause carrying its own *after*, not at the apodosis head, so the frame keeps *it was so ... that* and the apodosis waw is `unrepresented` under rule 14. The verse has the same shape as the rule's cited JOS.6 example. This restores the edge the verse pass had overridden.

BSB: no disagreement is a genuine error. The two v7 articles are rules 41 and 47 (the phrase writes one determiner and the demonstrative takes it); the v3 waw, the five `לְ`s and the v11 `אֹת` are the documented convention difference over function morphemes; the v8 `אִם` has no English written for it beside `כִּי`'s *for*; the v9 `פְּנֵי` is rule 30's contiguity condition applied to the `נָשָׂא פָּנִים` idiom, which the chapter fuses in v8 where the morphemes are contiguous. Nothing here was changed to move the aggregate.

Two constructions the chapter treats two ways on purpose, now recorded as conventions so a later pass does not read them as splits: the `נָשָׂא פָּנִים` idiom (fused in v8, split in v9 on contiguity), and JOB.42.3's two `וְלֹא` clauses (rule 46's headless *that which* against rule 17's bare *which* for a waw).

No promotion. The `וְעַתָּה` division follows from rules 11, 24, 25 and 51 as they already stand, so a new rule would restate them, and the precedent tables supplied carry no `עַתָּה` rows, so the precondition that the corpus agree is not met. A later chapter that has that evidence in hand can promote the division to rule 14; recording it as a chapter convention costs nothing in the meantime.
